
```{r}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

nhanes <- read_csv(
  "examples/nhanes-equity/data/nhanes_equity_v6.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)
```

```{r}
bmi_summary <- nhanes |>
  filter(
    !is.na(BMI),
    !is.na(IncomeGroup),
    !is.na(Cycle),
    !is.na(Age),
    Age >= 20,
    Age <= 80
  ) |>
  group_by(Cycle, IncomeGroup) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_bmi = mean(BMI),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(n >= 30)

bmi_summary
```

## Corrected Visualization

```{r}
corrected_plot <- ggplot(
  bmi_summary,
  aes(x = Cycle, y = mean_bmi,
      color = IncomeGroup, group = IncomeGroup)
) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  expand_limits(y = 26) +
  labs(
    title = "Mean BMI by Income Group Across NHANES Cycles",
    subtitle = "Adults aged 20–80; unweighted descriptive summary",
    x = "NHANES Cycle",
    y = "Mean BMI (kg/m²)",
    color = "Income Group",
    caption = "Prepared NHANES classroom dataset; descriptive and unweighted. \nMissing values excluded; groups with n < 30 removed."
  ) +
  theme_minimal()+
  coord_flip()
corrected_plot

ggsave("corrected-plot.png", plot = corrected_plot,
       width = 9, height = 6)
```

## Visual Audit and Revisions

The original plot used a narrow BMI axis without explaining how it could affect interpretation. My revised plot includes more NHANES cycles and uses coord_flip() to make the labels easier to read. I kept a zoomed BMI axis to show small differences between groups, but explained this choice in the caption.

I also changed the causal title to a descriptive one, filtered participants to ages 20–80, excluded missing values, and removed groups with fewer than 30 observations. The results are descriptive and unweighted, so they cannot establish causation or represent the US population.

## Interpretation and Limitations

This figure shows unweighted mean BMI by income group across NHANES cycles in the prepared classroom dataset. It is a descriptive comparison and does not establish causation or provide nationally representative estimates.
